top_stories.title: Fair electoral rolls lead to fair polls: CEC - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar** stated that fair electoral rolls are essential for fair elections, highlighting India's current state in this regard. **Kumar** praised the role of Booth Level Officers and Booth Level Agents in electoral roll management during his inaugural speech at the second National Conference of Counsels representing the **Election Commission of India**. He also congratulated electors from Assam, Kerala, Puducherry, Tamil Nadu, and West Bengal for their historic participation in recent Assembly elections.

top_stories.title: Mob attacks Trinamool leader Abhishek Banerjee; Mamata blames it on BJP - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Abhishek Banerjee**, general secretary of the **Trinamool Congress**, was attacked by a mob in Sonarpur, West Bengal on Saturday. The attack occurred during his visit to the residence of a party worker allegedly killed in post-poll violence.  The mob threw eggs and shoes at **Banerjee** as security personnel attempted to shield him from the crowd chanting "chor chor" (thief thief).

top_stories.title: West Bengal Cabinet expansion on June 1 - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Suvendu Adhikari**, the West Bengal Chief Minister, is expected to expand his Cabinet on June 1st and allocate key portfolios to senior **BJP** leaders. The first **BJP** Cabinet in the state will likely have over 30 members, with names announced after approval from the party's central leadership.  The selection criteria for the new ministers will consider seniority, regional representation, and experience, aiming to ensure inclusion of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, women, and representatives from northern and south western Bengal. The Cabinet expansion follows **Adhikari**'s recent swearing-in as a Minister and his oversight of 42 state departments.

top_stories.title: Senior Sri Lankan monk suspended over child sex abuse allegation | Crime News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Pallegama Hemarathana**, a senior Sri Lankan monk, has been suspended from his duties after being accused of sexually abusing an 11-year-old girl in 2022. The **Council of Monks of the Malwatte Chapter** took this rare disciplinary action following police arrest on May 9th. Hemarathana was detained at a private hospital in Colombo while awaiting legal proceedings.  The temple, where the alleged abuse occurred, draws thousands of visitors daily and is considered sacred to Buddhists.

top_stories.title: Defence Minister inaugurates ‘Nausena Shaurya Vatika’ in Lucknow - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Rajnath Singh**, **Yogi Adityanath**, and others jointly inaugurated the ‘Nausena Shaurya Vatika’, an open-air naval museum in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh.  The museum is a second phase of the Nausena Shaurya Sangrahalaya, showcasing the Indian Navy's history and valor. **Singh** praised the Navy's role in Operation Sindoor, highlighting its pressure on Pakistan during the operation. He also commended the progress of Uttar Pradesh under **Adityanath**, attributing it to strong law and order and a shift from "goonda raj" to a focus on development and investment.

top_stories.title: ‘Opposite visions’: What to know about Colombia’s presidential election | Elections News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: The upcoming presidential election in Colombia is shaping up to be a contest between two opposing visions for the country's future. **Senator Ivan Cepeda**, leading the left-wing candidates, has emerged as the frontrunner, promising continuity with President Gustavo Petro’s policies while advocating for a "Total Peace" approach to resolving the country's internal conflict.  The right wing is facing a fractured field of candidates, including Abelardo de la Espriella and Paloma Valencia, who offer contrasting approaches to security and economic issues. De la Espriella advocates for a hardline security model, while Valencia proposes a more moderate approach with increased police presence and pro-business policies. The election will be crucial as it marks the first time Colombia has held a presidential election since its first leftist president took office.

top_stories.title: D.K. Shivakumar meets Governor Gehlot, stakes claim to form new govt in Karnataka - The Hindu
top_stories.rephrased_article: **D.K. Shivakumar**, the newly elected leader of the **Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee**, will be sworn in as Chief Minister on Wednesday, June 3rd at Lok Bhavan. The event is expected to be attended by the central leadership of the party and Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot has invited him to take the oath at 4:05 p.m.  The power transition was overseen by **Mallikarjun Kharge**, **Rahul Gandhi**, and **Sonia Gandhi**.  With Cabinet formation still under discussion, speculation remains about whether a full Cabinet will be sworn in and if there will be deputy Chief Ministers.

top_stories.title: Romania: Residents shaken after Russian drone strike
top_stories.rephrased_article: A Russian drone strike injured two people in a building near the Romanian-Ukrainian border, prompting fear among residents. **Romanian President Nicușor Dan** stated that the drone was likely intercepted by Ukrainian air defenses over Kyiv's territory, while **Moscow** disputed this claim.

top_stories.title: Confirmed Ebola cases nearly double in days as WHO chief visits DR Congo | Ebola News | Al Jazeera
top_stories.rephrased_article: **WHO** director-general Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus visited the epicenter of a deadly Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), urging community involvement in combating the disease. Confirmed cases nearly doubled in two days, reaching 225 on Friday, and the outbreak is spreading rapidly through conflict-hit regions. The **Africa CDC** reports global funding for the response has significantly decreased, while **Doctors Without Borders** warns that the response has not kept pace with the outbreak's severity.  The WHO is working to assess experimental drugs and a candidate vaccine, and regional countries are on alert, closing borders with DRC.

top_stories.title: Is Melania Trump an 'alien'? Indian-origin attorney says White House's immigrant-bashing crosses line - The Times of India
top_stories.rephrased_article: **Rahul Reddy**, an Indian-origin immigration attorney, criticized the use of the word "alien" by **the White House**, arguing that it is dehumanizing and fuels negative perceptions.  He pointed out that while the term is legal in immigration law, its usage by the White House creates a narrative that paints lawful immigrants as outsiders. Reddy questioned if **Melania Trump**, who was born in Slovenia, is also an alien, highlighting the hypocrisy of using such language when the President's own family has a history of immigration.
